text:
sana: Heads up — canary shows inconsistent read-after-write for tenant snapshots when we demote a hot prefix. Seen this twice in the last hour. anyone else?

liam: repro steps? logs?

sana: quick paste of repro trace:
```
[2026-03-21T10:12:01Z] demote prefix pfx_42 epoch=137 -> mark demote_inflight
[2026-03-21T10:12:01Z] write tenant A key k1 v1 epoch=138 ack
[2026-03-21T10:12:01Z] read tenant A key k1 returns stale v0 epoch=136
```

alex: that looks like read path is skipping `epoch` check when demote_inflight is set. we might be hitting an ownership window where snapshot version advances but cache demotion hasn't completed.

maya: are we mismatching snapshot vs commit epoch? if demote just flags the prefix and eviction runs async, reads could land on a slab that hasn't seen the latest apply. :thinking:

noah: locking-wise we avoid global locks for perf. adding sync would kill tail latency. prefer a light-weight guard + retry.

dana: +1 on retry. two ideas: 1) optimistic epoch compare on read (if read epoch < tenant epoch then retry with backoff), or 2) bump a per-prefix `stable_epoch` once demote fully completes and have read require stable_epoch >= seen_epoch.

liam: option 1 is cheaper to implement but risk more retries on hot keys. option 2 needs additional metadata but gives deterministic correctness.

vincent: we should measure how often this happens before choosing. canary rate is ~0.2% of reads right now.

maya: can we do a small hybrid: keep optimistic epoch compare + a quick bounded backoff (like 2-3 attempts with jitter up to 30ms) and then fall back to a strong check that consults `prefix_stable_epoch`?

noah: that seems reasonable. latency hit will be tiny for the majority. put a counter for retry-induced latency.

sana: implementation sketch: on demote start set `demote_inflight=true`. readers do: read_epoch = slab.epoch; if read_epoch < tenant_commit_epoch -> sleep jitter; retry up to N. if still stale, check `prefix_stable_epoch` (strong guard) and block until stable or time out. demote completion increments `prefix_stable_epoch` and clears inflight.

alex: one caveat: strong guard must not block long-running GC/compaction. cap wait to e.g., 200ms and surface metric.

dana: also record a per-prefix metric `demote_retries` and `demote_block_ms`. ops can set alert if retries spike.

vincent: add tracing tags so we can correlate read trace -> demote event. please include `prefix_id` and `epoch_seen`.

liam: agree on metrics/tracing. want canary target: 0.05% user-visible stale reads and P99 extra latency < 8ms for reads that hit retry path.

sana: i'll draft a small PR that adds optimistic retry + fallback check + metrics. will also add smoke test to canary that demotes a prefix while doing tight read/write loop.

alex: assign owner and rollout plan?

sana: owner = sana. PI: small canary (10%), watch `demote_retries`, `demote_block_ms`, `stale_read_rate`. if canary looks clean roll to 100%.

noah: please add kill-switch config: `prefix_demote_strict_mode=false` default. ops can flip it for emergency.

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: sana/kv-demote-retry-mitigation -> canary (10%) at 2026-03-21T11:00:00Z by sana.

vincent: thanks. can you also add a follow-up RFC for the long-term plan to remove demote_inflight race by making demote a synchronous transition in the control plane? want to discuss tradeoffs next week.

sana: noted, will put an RFC on the agenda. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
